findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. The names count_up_to, limit, total, place, lower, current, and higher expose prefix counting and the three positional components directly. The zero-specific branch is compact without obscuring leading-placeholder exclusion, and there is no exact generic local named index.

Prefix subtraction count_up_to(high) - count_up_to(low - 1) leaves exactly the inclusive range. At each decimal place, higher counts complete cycles, current selects the partial-cycle case, and lower determines the exact equal-digit tail. For nonzero d, higher * place plus zero, place, or lower + 1 counts every written occurrence at that position. For d = 0, requiring higher > 0 excludes positions absent from shorter representations, subtracting one complete cycle removes leading-zero placeholders, and the current-zero partial cycle adds lower + 1. Each written decimal position belongs to exactly one such contribution, and a nonpositive prefix correctly contributes zero.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 1067, Python, and the native digitsCount(d, low, high) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms one digit d from 0 through 9 and inclusive positive bounds satisfying 1 <= low <= high <= 2 * 10^8. The app-local solve adapter preserves ordinary decimal representations without leading zeros, separate counting of repeated positions in one number, both range endpoints, and the integer occurrence-total return contract.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2067482233 are algorithmically identical: both count prefixes through the same decimal place loop, compute the same lower/current/higher split, apply the same nonzero cycle formula, remove the same leading-zero cycle for d = 0, and subtract the low - 1 prefix from high. Their only structural difference is the required Solution.digitsCount wrapper.

The three hidden workloads extend the inclusive range from 1..100 through 1..10000 while preserving simple exact expected counts. The exact protected source passed all ten visible correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent -0.00 and a 1.00x largest runtime ratio. An independently correct range enumerator matched every correctness and benchmark output but failed only the calibrated complexity verdict at +0.82 and 73.52x, distinguishing O(log H) positional arithmetic from enumeration proportional to the range and written digits.

The Approach accurately derives prefix subtraction, the higher/current/lower decomposition, complete and partial cycles for nonzero digits, and the special leading-zero correction. It covers a one-number range, repeated digits, powers of ten, digit zero, and a prefix below one. The O(log H) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The modular Reference states the single target digit, positive inclusive range, endpoint inclusion, per-position multiplicity, and ordinary decimal notation without leading-zero placeholders. It preserves the two source examples in order with both explanations, places the useful zero case under Additional Examples, records both constraints and both source hints, and introduces no unsupported source-native section.

A fresh authenticated review of the live Premium statement verified exactly two explained examples, two constraints, two hints, and no statement images, tables, diagrams, notes, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds the independently written modular Reference to live content hash 197c7913c59c1da8a7d999b3e95c4a33d4b48b1b58ba699b13906e79754dbb02 and validates with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Their exact inputs and outputs appear first in source order; the former third sample is now correctly labeled as an additional zero-semantics trial.

All ten ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials. They cover digit endpoints 0 and 9, low = 1, high = 2 * 10^8, low = high, short and wide inclusive intervals, and every contract relation between the two bounds.

Material behavior includes excluding omitted leading zeros, repeated occurrences within one number, no occurrences, crossing a decimal-width boundary, complete tens and ones cycles, narrow prefix subtraction, crossing a power of ten, and eight written zeros at the maximum upper bound.

An independent tight digit-DP oracle tracks position, tightness, and whether the number has started, returning both the number of positive representations and their target-digit occurrences. Its explicit started state excludes leading placeholders without using the protected higher/current/lower formula.

The oracle, protected app source, and immutable native Solution agreed on all 13 authored correctness-plus-benchmark inputs, 50500 exhaustive choices of d and 1 <= low <= high <= 100, and 5000 deterministic random legal ranges through 200000000. A direct range enumerator also matched all 13 authored outputs.

The 100-, 1000-, and 10000-value workloads remain hidden and performance-only, use size consistently as the inclusive upper bound and range extent from 1, and span 100x. The correct enumerator failed only scaling at +0.82 and 73.52x, while the O(log H) protected source passed at -0.00 and 1.00x.
